notes.title: Wizard of Legend 2 Leaves Early Access June 12th
notes.notes:
Get ready to unleash your magical prowess and embark on an electrifying new journey in [b]Wizard of Legend 2, launching into 1.0 worldwide on June 12, 2025[/b]. After being in Early Access since October 2024, the 1.0 version of Wizard of Legend 2 will come to PC, PlayStation, and Xbox adding new content like the Chaos Biome, Chaos minibosses, and a formidable Final Boss. Players can also master 12 new Chaos Arcana, discover 10 new relics, and take on fresh objectives with new contracts. With expanded multiplayer options for local and online co-op, the update builds on the fast-paced, spell-based combat, offering an even more vibrant, action-packed world.


The 1.0 update brings a wealth of gameplay enhancements that increase replayability and challenge. Players can now face the ultimate trial in the Chaos Biome, where they'll battle minibosses and the new Final Boss. With over 75 Arcana to master, including the Chaos Arcana, players can experiment with different elemental combinations to craft their unique playstyle.


The addition of achievements, new contracts, and customization options ensures that every playthrough feels fresh and rewarding. Whether teaming up with friends for 4-player co-op or facing the trials alone, Wizard of Legend 2 offers endless strategic possibilities. The update also includes numerous bug fixes, optimizations, and balance adjustments to make the game smoother and more polished than ever before.


[b]Wizard of Legend 2 features added since Early Access:[/b]
[list]
[*] 4-player Co-op: Team up with friends in seamless online or local multiplayer, supporting up to four players. Online and local co-op gameplay has been enhanced with better responsiveness for Arcana abilities, refined camera behavior, multiplayer boss HP adjustments, and smoother item selection to reduce accidental purchases, resulting in a more gratifying co-op experience.

[*] Chaos Biome and New Challenges: The addition of the Chaos Biome introduces fresh environments, new minibosses, and a formidable Final Boss, providing dynamic combat encounters and serving as the ultimate trial. 

[*] Master Elemental Arcana: Players can master the element of Chaos with 12 new Arcana, offering additional magical powers and new strategies to explore.

[*] New Contracts: Take on a brand new batch of objectives with new contracts, earning rewards as you progress.

[*] Sky Citadel Content Update: The Sky Citadel content update introduced a new biome with 12 new enemies, including the Royal Spear Knight miniboss and the King and Queen boss. Along with the return of Dash Arcana, including 15 Arcana options, two new NPCs, improved boss behaviors, updated dialogues and voice lines, enhanced customization, local co-op improvements, and numerous balance changes.

[*] Gameplay Improvements: Thanks to player feedback, the team has implemented several quality-of-life improvements since Early Access, including numerous fixes and tweaks to enhance gameplay, such as smoother local and online co-op, bug fixes for Arcana and Relic interactions, better boss behavior, and refined level designs. Adjustments also addressed UI issues, menu improvements, and balance changes to ensure a more polished and enjoyable experience.

[*] Expanded Language Support: Wizard of Legend 2 supports a wide array of languages including Brazilian Portuguese, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Russian, Spanish, and Turkish, expanding accessibility for players worldwide.
[/list]

Be sure to follow developer Dead Mage on [url=https://x.com/deadmagestudio]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/deadmage]Facebook[/url], and [url=https://www.instagram.com/deadmagi/]Instagram[/url], as well as visit the [url=https://deadmage.com/]official website[/url]. Join the community and begin your adventure to become the next Wizard of Legend!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/97dfe5da87ed50a39674180fe68348f771c265a6.jpg[/img]

Here’s what you can expect to see throughout Early Access (please note these features are listed in no particular order):


[b]1. New Biomes: Castle and the Final Biome[/b]

Prepare to explore entirely new environments! We’re working on introducing two distinct biomes—Castle and the Final Biome—each offering:
[list]
[*] Unique environments: Visually stunning environments filled with new obstacles to overcome.
[*] Unique enemies: Face fresh challenges as you battle foes never before seen in the trials.
[*] Epic boss fights: Each biome will culminate in an intense boss battle that will test your skills.
[/list]
[b]2. Two New Elemental Bosses[/b]

We’re adding even more depth to the elemental challenges with two new elemental adversaries that will bring their distinct Arcana to the trials offering fresh challenges and rewards

[list]
[*] Fire Boss: Brace yourself for an inferno of fiery attacks and scorching strategies.
[*] Wind Boss: A master of the skies, this boss will push your mastery of Arcana to new heights.
[/list]
[b]3. Expanded Narrative and Story[/b]

The trials have always been more than just tests of power. As we continue to expand the Wizard of Legend 2 world, we’ll introduce more profound lore and story elements. This will include:
The story of other wizards in the trials: Discover more about the characters you meet, their motivations, and the greater mysteries behind the trials.

[b]4. More Arcana, Variants and Enhancements[/b]

Expect an even more extensive arsenal of Arcana spells to discover and wield, adding layers of strategy and gameplay variety. Enhance your favorite Arcana with new upgrades, allowing you to fine-tune and power up your spells to suit your preferred strategy. Experiment with new elemental powers and craft unique combinations that suit your combat style.

[b]5. More Relics[/b]

As the trials progress, we’ll introduce more powerful relics that offer buffs, unique abilities, and new ways to tailor your wizard's abilities. Keep an eye out for relics that can dramatically alter the course of your run!

[b]6. 4-Player Co-op[/b]

One of the most requested features is coming! We’re working on expanding the co-op experience from two players to four-player co-op, letting you and three friends team up for even more chaotic and exciting multiplayer action.

[b]8. More Medallions[/b]

We’re also expanding the collection of Medallions—items that have distinct gameplay effects and can change the way you approach the trials. Look out for new medallions that can give your wizard the edge in battle.

[b]9. More Contracts[/b]

Expect more Contracts to be added, which are special objectives requested by members of the hub. Managed by Aletheia, these contracts will allow you to delve deeper into the lore of the world while earning unique rewards.

[b]10. More Customization Options[/b]

Show off your unique style! We’re adding more cosmetic customization options, including masks, robes, and symbols. Customize your wizard’s appearance to stand out as you take on the trials.

[b]11. More Charms and Difficulty Settings[/b]

For wizards seeking greater challenges, we're introducing an expanded range of Charms and Difficulty Settings. These features will allow you to customize your gameplay experience and push your skills to the limit:
[list]
[*] New Charms: Unlock powerful modifiers that alter gameplay mechanics, enemy behavior, or environmental factors, creating fresh and demanding scenarios.
[*] Adjustable Difficulty Levels: Fine-tune the intensity of your trials with more granular difficulty options, catering to both newcomers and seasoned wizards.
[/list]

These additions will provide endless replayability and ensure that even the most experienced wizards will find new ways to test their mastery of the arcane arts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/29baac8e564c0dbc34270d90f2ae2beb5e372e5c.jpg[/img]

Throughout Early Access, we’ll refine the core gameplay and balance combat for you to experiment with. Your feedback plays a crucial role in helping us shape the future of Wizard of Legend 2, so keep sharing your thoughts as you take on the trials!

Thank you for being part of this journey. We can’t wait to see how you harness the power of the elements!

Stay magical,
The Wizard of Legend 2 Team

notes.title: Mastering the Elements - A Look at Arcana in Wizard of Legend 2
notes.notes:
Hello Wizards!

As we dive into developing the sequel, we wanted to share a bit about our journey so far. It’s both an honor and a challenge to build on the foundation of a game so many of you love. We’re working hard to honor the legacy of the first game while also bringing fresh ideas to the table for a new generation of players. It’s all about finding that sweet spot between keeping the charm of the original and exploring new gameplay mechanics, art styles, and storytelling techniques.

One of the exciting aspects of this sequel is how we’re weaving lore into the experience. Players will uncover fascinating details about the elemental forces and the mysterious figures behind the trials. But don’t worry—the story is designed to enhance your journey rather than dictate how you play. It’s all about action and exploration, letting you uncover the narrative at your own pace!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/515e0bac80f449cb6f153c09b9f8650e02f4990c.png[/img]

[b]Harnessing the Elements and the Power of Arcana[/b]
Let’s talk about Arcana! Players can tap into various elemental powers like Fire, Wind, Earth, Water, Lightning, and even Chaos. Each element comes with its own unique spells and playstyles—think explosive fireballs, swirling wind currents, and earth-shattering attacks. And with the Chaos Arcana, expect some unpredictable twists that really shake things up! The diversity in these elements gives you tons of options for both offense and defense, letting you tailor your strategy to your liking.

In Wizard of Legend 2, you can look forward to some brand-new Arcana that push the boundaries of elemental magic. We drew inspiration from a mix of mythology and classic fantasy, all while focusing on evolving our combat mechanics. We want you to feel powerful in your gameplay, but also to have a rich tactical experience. Many new abilities come with unique effects—like chaining lightning between enemies or manipulating the terrain with earth-based spells.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/1015411c860befa64a286facdac406b805498f06.gif[/img]

One of the coolest features is the ability to mix and match Arcana to create powerful combos. The game really shines in the experimentation department, letting you discover synergies between different spells. Whether you’re stunning enemies with Earth Arcana and following up with a fiery blast, or choosing from a myriad of other spell combinations, you’ll have the freedom to explore strategies that fit your playstyle.

We believe community feedback is crucial during our Early Access phase, and we’re eager to hear from you! Your insights on balance, content, and features will help us refine the game. You can connect with us through the official [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2193540/discussions/]Steam forums[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/XFdenm5qkt]Discord[/url], and our social media channels. We’ll be actively monitoring these platforms to understand your thoughts and suggestions, and we’re committed to making meaningful changes based on your experiences. Your voice matters!

Thanks for joining us on this journey. We can’t wait to share more with you as we continue developing Wizard of Legend 2!

notes.title: Wizard of Legend 2 - Community Driven Changes
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/697c767db720a780fd7e60fbd90cf2068367aa7b.png[/img]

We’d like to thank you all for the awesome feedback we got on the Demo of Wizard of Legend 2 at SteamNextFest. Your comments gave us the perspective we needed to rework the game.

We’ll keep listening to your voices throughout Early Access and we’ll continue refining Wizard of Legend 2 based on your experiences. Share your thoughts and help us make the most of this period to produce the best game possible.

[b]Our New Narrative Direction[/b]

After listening to your feedback at SteamNextFest, we have overhauled the narrative completely. You now play as a single wizard rather than a parade of randomly generated wizards. We’ve built a basic narrative framework for the version you’re playing now—just enough to give the game some context—but we haven’t dived deep into storytelling yet. 

Our plan is to gradually expand the story through monthly updates, where we’ll explore the exciting journey of the wizards in the Trials of Legend. More news on the rivalries, friendships, and conflicts you’ll find on the road to becoming the Wizard of Legend will be coming soon!

We have significantly reduced the commentary and changed the tone and style of it according to the wishes of our players. And yes, we brought back the Elemental Boss puns—you asked, and we listened! 

Let us know if the new balance of humor, mentorship, and character-specific banter fits your expectations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/13f95bbcbab2a3a845ac27774d1ab393555159ad.gif[/img]

[b]What We’ve Updated[/b]

All of you at SteamNextFest had plenty of comments about features that are currently in-progress, and we’d like to reply to some of them here. First, we’ve added a ton quality of life updates that all our fans should appreciate.

We revamped the progression system to make it even more rewarding for both casual and hardcore players. The core structure of this system is in the game and we look forward to refining it based on your feedback.

Exploration should make more sense now. We wanted to see more players enjoy exploring the trials, so we added a map, a mini-map, and larger levels. The result should make it easier to venture through the biomes. However, be warned: we also tweaked enemy behaviors and made the game slightly more difficult. Breezing through the demo does not guarantee you an easy time here.

As requested, we’ve added in customization. Wizard of Legend 2 now features a treasure trove of cloaks, symbols, and masks for you to wear. And we’ve also added in a new medallion system that affects gameplay, just like the outfits in the first game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/7d5aabcc5e0402aebaca257a043ac0b4c984212b.gif[/img]

[b]What Else?[/b]

We have improved the feel of Arcana, tweaked how enemies pullback on hit, and updated the sound effects for most Arcana. In fact, we updated the game’s music entirely to better match the feel of the trials and world. Delving through the trials to the new soundtrack will be a magical experience.

We also updated the hub layout to make its functions more visible and provided some general improvements. Hopefully, you’ll have a good time navigating the Trials Mansion.

We also heard your feedback about dash Arcana and are currently considering whether it’s feasible to add them in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/84bc855b27bb1db7f9fef759f3510105a1b9292a.gif[/img]

Thanks for being an essential part of this journey. We can’t wait to see where you take Wizard of Legend 2 with your feedback!

Take care,

Dead Mage

notes.title: Almost Legendary – When Ice and Lightning Strike
notes.notes:
In [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2193540/Wizard_of_Legend_2/]Wizard of Legend 2[/url][/b], would-be legends from across Lanova assemble to test their skills in the trials of the Floating Lands. Each brings their unique strategies, elemental proclivities, and mix of powerful Arcana to prove to the Wizard Council they’re the best of the best of the best. Some will skirt success. Most will fail spectacularly.
 
In this first installment of [b]Almost Legendary[/b], we chronicle the tale and tactics of one such contender who could have become a legend…but instead will go down in history as just another pretender.

[h1]Chilling Shock[/h1]

[h3]Wizard of Origin: Maestro, the superconductor
Cause of Defeat: Mis-timed double dash into the void[/h3]

This particularly devious wizard built his fate around the [b]Lighting Conductor[/b] Relic, which massively increases lighting damage on frozen enemies. (If you see it as a starting choice in your run, get ready to bring the pain!) Maestro then chose the [b]Ice Blast[/b] Signature Arcana, which freezes enemies in a small cone in front of you on a brief cooldown. Since he planned to battle up close, he chose [b]Lightning Spinner[/b], which works like a fast-hitting electric flail, as his Basic Arcana. (Unleash it with abandon and watch your frozen foes sizzle to a crisp.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/8845c6d47271c44f70319f333135be69e1ccf2f5.gif[/img]

In keeping with the theme of “up close and personal,” the Signature Arcana [b]Galvanizing Discharge[/b] buffets enemies around you with a thunderous blast and knocks them back, though any other Lighting-based Standard Arcana will be effective if you choose to try this yourself.

Two Relics gave this build that extra oomph he sought: [b]Battery of Tanaris[/b], which grants yet another boost to your Lightning damage, and [b]Arctic Gloves[/b], which keeps enemies frozen longer. If you manage to get this setup rolling yourself, you’ll almost feel sorry for the inhabitants of the Labyrinth. Just learn from Maestro, and don’t let all that lightning prevent you from spotting the pits.

[h2]Wizard’s Arsenal[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/9dd45a55c7b2a272db8ecaf171fe891480cea4ae.png[/img]

[i]Developer’s Notes: “Ice Blast is a versatile Standard Arcana that can benefit all kinds of builds. In this instance, its confined area-of-effect synergizes with the other close-range Arcana, but it would be just as useful as a disengagement tool in builds where you want to stay at longer range. When fully charged, it becomes immensely useful as a means to reset the battlefield.  –Game Director Aryan Bina[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/9e46f067a5e1ae02c9003e39259a4ae9b9f5220a.gif[/img]

[i]Wizard of Legend 2 is currently in development, so aspects of the gameplay previewed here might change before release—and Dead Mage is always interested in hearing your feedback! notes.notes:
In the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2193540/view/4155212136883602555]third Arcane Knowledge mini-series entry[/url], we explored developer Dead Mage’s roots and what the studio's earlier game Children of Morta taught the team about storytelling. For our fourth and final entry in this mini-series, let’s talk a little more about how…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/f8a563557b6ec73ac3bb16b5b03b64a24e6bea58.png[/img]

[h3]Story matters[/h3]

As is evident from the studio’s previous work, Dead Mage clearly takes storytelling seriously. The rogue-lite genre presents both distinct challenges and opportunities, and the team is hard at work implementing a narrative approach that leverages its strengths—and doubles-down on what makes Wizard of Legend unique.

“We’ve gone all-in on the world of Lanova,” says game director Aryan Bina. “Fans of the original will recognize some old faces,” such as the shadowy purveyor of cursed relics, Nox, “and we’re introducing many more who we hope that they’ll love just as much.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/c223df83a824fce8a2f01aa2d883057da0f805ba.png[/img]
Wizard of Legend 2 weaves a tale from an earlier era of Lanova, centered around a cast of characters who each have different reasons for being at Van Eyckrous mansion. Head mage Hieronymus wants to discover someone worthy of becoming the next Wizard of Legend. The powerful sorcerer Serjik can’t resist the siren’s song of a good challenge. Madam Moulin, Nazradin, and Aletheia each have their own tales to discover.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/51b8a8366b76241b26e84331be5fe59e69ec122c.jpg[/img]

“In the spirit of the game’s fast pace, these characters will be the primary vehicles for storytelling—they’ll move the plot along and give you insights about the world as you play, and when you talk to them in the hub. This being a rogue-lite game that you can play for many hours, you should expect lots of story in here, as well as some unexpected twists.”

As for what awaits those who seek to become a legend, the wizards of Lanova will have to find out for themselves...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/f02419a4a23cc0b302c9bdff8158ca540bafe752.png[/img]

Following up the original Wizard of Legend is a charge that Dead Mage doesn’t take lightly. The game was a certified hit, with a community of passionate players across multiple platforms—and Dead Mage is committed to honoring that for the sequel. 

“We’re all huge fans of the original Wizard of Legend,” says Bina. “For us, success means staying true to what made it great, and giving fans more of that. Feedback from the community is a huge help for us in achieving this.”

To be part of that conversation and stay up to date on Wizard of Legend 2, wishlist the game here on Steam, and join us on [url=https://x.com/wizardoflegend2]X[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/WizardOfLegend/]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/wizardoflegend2/]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@wizardoflegend2]TikTok[/url], and [url=https://discord.com/invite/aXuVtzzt]Discord[/url].

notes.title: Arcane Knowledge 3: Learning from a legacy
notes.notes:
In our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2193540/view/4155212136883598066]previous Arcane Knowledge mini-series entry[/url], you learned more about how death is a great teacher (but meta-progression upgrades are pretty great too). Today, we’ll explore another excellent teacher—your own past experiences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/e94a923667dab9aa4c627edb6784d7202ea5f7a3.png[/img]

[h3]Children of Morta’s DNA runs deep through Wizard of Legend 2[/h3]

Prior to working on Wizard of Legend 2, Dead Mage created [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/330020/Children_of_Morta/]Children of Morta[/url], an acclaimed rogue-lite action RPG lauded for its carefully crafted and expansive story, stellar gameplay, and engrossing progression loop. Now the team is thrilled to have the spirited, Arcana-infused world of Lanova as their canvas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/f60209836aaaf2342d534d6ef7a7e450e778a10d.jpg[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/4afe216be63c4f07449f75689288b80f41b52119.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/f6b266169e3d3368c31b12c71b3d9a3fb009223b.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/2539b1eda9688e5bf4f6a28c042bf7ae02bac2e2.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/4128e3f8f4bcbc546e589e697ba1c0e2b1426510.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/2ef318407ea2cf419983d9b276858011593fcca4.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/3c51faa0de8c3767942f091c3b1f95da070489c3.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/cedd7650b3d094fc9974e10d5558eb5fab987d9d.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/620c6d66304aaa596430d097db5f68acf8c83d81.jpg[/img][/url]

“Children of Morta taught us a ton about integrating story into a rogue-lite game,” says game director Aryan Bina. “We're building on what we learned, but with a greater emphasis on procedural storytelling in Wizard of Legend 2. Our goal is to preserve the original game’s fast pace, so we’ve put a lot of effort into making sure we can effectively convey the story through in-game commentary from the main characters.”

Cooperative multiplayer came as a post-release update to Children of Morta, and adding such a substantial feature to an already established game was a challenge. Dead Mage took that experience to heart for Wizard of Legend 2, which will launch with local and online co-op supporting up to four players. 

“We’re designing Wizard of Legend 2 with multiplayer in mind from the outset,” Bina says. “From building strong network architecture, to working out all sorts of gameplay-related details—stuff like multiplayer game balance, visibility and readability—these are all things that we’ve been lucky enough to be able to address as soon as we started the project. Our intention is to make Wizard of Legend 2 as fun and balanced in groups as it is playing solo.”

notes.title: Arcane Knowledge 2: Facing the inevitable
notes.notes:
In our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2193540/view/4155212136883381979]previous Arcane Knowledge mini-series[/url] entry, you learned more about Arcana and the enhancements you can apply to them. Wise wizards learn to master the combinations available to them. But most wizards aren’t wise, and they will learn today’s lesson the hard way…

[h3]Death is inevitable (but progression is permanent)[/h3]

There’s no way around it: you will die a lot while playing Wizard of Legend 2. Ascending to the pinnacle of arcane prestige is not supposed to be easy! But the good news is that you—well, technically, the endless parade of ambitious wizards you’ll guide through the trials of the Floating Lands—will only get better after each death.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/a3651b062360541daa3f75b203f10f0de0c30675.png[/img]

One of the first things you’ll notice upon visiting Van Eyckrous mansion, the game’s hub area, is a wondrous magical apparatus with a seemingly insatiable appetite for the Chaos Gems you’ll collect during your runs. The more of them you feed it, the more permanent upgrades it will bestow upon you to aid in future runs.

“One primary upgrade available through the apparatus is the Double Dash," says game director Aryan Bina, calling out a power the team expects will be an early must-pick for many players. “This allows wizards to execute a second dash immediately after the first, which is particularly useful for traversing pits.” The Floating Lands are littered with pits, and being able to dash over them in dual succession is both liberating and life-saving.

Aspirants with a flair for fashion will also be thrilled to learn that robes are making a return from the original Wizard of Legend. Switching up your wardrobe is not only good for morale, but each robe also confers powerful gameplay benefits. “Some robes are designed specifically to assist players less experienced in this genre,” says Bina, and will be helpful for beginner wizards who may just be coming to grips with the rogue-lite hazards of the Floating Lands.

notes.title: Arcane Knowledge 1: Magic possibilities of Wizard of Legend 2
notes.notes:
Bold and ambitious mages, whose eyes are set on wizardly prestige—welcome to [b]Arcane Knowledge[/b], a mini-series of mini-articles exploring a few fascinating facets of the fast-paced rogue-lite’s development, from its renewed emphasis on character-driven storytelling to its expanded options for build-crafting.

[i]What secrets shall we scry?[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/5ae1bae50f0abe9d7c7db68ec53cc09938222d8b.png[/img]

[h3]More magic = more better[/h3]

Wielding the elements in all their destructive majesty is what the Wizard of Legend experience is all about—and this is precisely what Dead Mage is aiming to build on in Wizard of Legend 2. The goal is to give you the widest possible palette of magical tools to experiment with as you assemble your ideal arsenal of [b]Arcana[/b], the spells you wield during your runs.

As we discussed in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2193540/view/7129836059820396996]Legendary Wizarding 101 preview[/url], wizards will start each run by choosing a loadout of Basic, Signature, and Standard Arcana from six elemental schools, with opportunities to acquire even more during their trials—but your Arcana will continue to evolve as you get further into your run.

“A big priority for us was to add a variety of enhancements that players can apply to each Arcana,” says Aryan Bina, game director of Wizard of Legend 2. “We want to offer players interesting choices for every Arcana. We’re hoping that this variety will encourage players to experiment and find clever and unexpected applications for their favorites.”

Bina conjures up [b]Dragon Dive[/b], a ranged Arcana, as an example of how enhancements can change your play. “It summons tunneling dragons to repel enemies, but its enhancements offer different strategies. [b]Dragon Ride[/b] allows the player to teleport at the end of the dragons, facilitating rapid repositioning and enemy confusion. For those who prefer a combination of melee and ranged combat, you could choose the [b]Returning Dragon[/b] enhancement, which performs a distant attack and pulls enemies closer for melee Arcana attacks.”

Factor in Arcana upgrades (which are applied independently from enhancements) as well as Relics (powerful ability-altering items that are returning from from the original Wizard of Legend) and you have a dizzying array of arcane build-crafting ahead of you. 

And of course, Wizard of Legend veterans should expect some all-new Arcana in the magical mix. Some of Dead Mage’s favorites include [b]Earthclap[/b], a thunderous area-of-effect ability that’s good for grouping-up enemies for further comboing, and [b]Monk Strike[/b], a fast-hitting close-range attack that’ll surely become a standby for melee mages.

notes.title: Legendary Wizarding 101: Chronicling Wizard of Legend 2’s Trials
notes.notes:
Dodging a rival wizard’s torrent of fire. Picking up the Cursed Relic that turns the tide against that accursed golem. Fleeting victory! Embarrassing, pit-based defeat. 

When a would-be Wizard of Legend bets their life to claim the Chalice of Immortality, the only thing certain is uncertainty. But that doesn’t mean you can’t be prepared for the chaos that awaits in developer Dead Mage’s upcoming action-packed rogue-lite dungeon crawler.

Today, let’s delve into what a typical solo trial might look like for the brave, foolish, magical contenders of [b]Wizard of Legend 2[/b]…

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2193540/Wizard_of_Legend_2/

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/4c4ed185fc7979494129e090e5cf8d381db2f28d.png[/img]

[h3]Legends of Lanova[/h3]

In an era long before the events of the original Wizard of Legend, a rare solar eclipse heralds the return of one of Lanova’s most ancient traditions: the legendary Trials, in which wizards from across the realm vie for their shot at life everlasting.

Only one wizard at a time can live with this immortal boon, an honor that currently belongs to a decadent, reclusive master of the arcane arts called Hieronymus. Together with his Wizard Council—the wise and disciplined Madam Moulin, the gravity-tending geomancer Nazradin, and the powerful and headstrong Serjik—they will test these ambitious young challengers to the Chalice, and find out whether any of them are worthy of becoming a legend. They certainly have their doubts.

[h3]Before the Storm[/h3]

Each trial begins with you choosing [b]1 of 3 random wizards[/b] to take on the upcoming trial from beginning to end. Each contender has a particular penchant or power granted by their starting Relic, such as a watery shield that deflects projectiles, or an affinity for Dragon Arcana. Maybe you’ll choose a favorite you’re familiar with. Maybe you’ll choose something outside your comfort zone. Just don’t get too attached to your sorcerous new friend.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/f1d0c5da63a57f32de847bf974f77b097e44c570.png[/img]

Before each wizard ventures into the Floating Lands (the gauntlet where Hieronymus hosts the Trials), you’ll first have a chance to explore the grand grounds of Van Eyckrous mansion, a hub of social and story activity where you’ll make some critical decisions for your run.

Here, you might chat with fellow wizard NPCs to hear about their brilliant (ahem) combat plans, engage Serjik or Hieronymus for sage advice or savage mockery, or strike up a conversation about the meaning of existence with some enchanted cleaning supplies. In this liminal space, the story advances between trials, as you learn more about the personalities, histories, secrets, and motivations that drive Wizard of Legend 2’s eccentric arcane assemblage.

Van Eyckrous mansion also plays host to a mystical Apparatus tended to by a young woman named Aletheia, Madam Moulin’s niece, conscripted to a life of monotonous maintenance due to her lack of magical talent. Wise wizards would do well to get on Aletheia’s good side, because the Apparatus could hold the key to ultimate success.

When a wizard feeds [b]Chaos Gems[/b] into this machine, it grants [b]permanent upgrades[/b] to the player—for example, making it so passing through portals rejuvenates health, or increasing the odds of discovering enhancements during your trials. These upgrades put the “-lite” in this rogue-lite, as they persist between each run; meaning when your current wizard falls in combat, the next wizards in line will be able to benefit from these upgrades, too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/ff5594f7b25446a63341998b92bb50a97445032a.png[/img]

[h3]Arcana Overwhelming![/h3]

Fire. Earth. Water. Air. Lightning. Chaos. Arcana are the source of every wizard’s power. The potential combinations are infinitely tantalizing. The opportunities for experimentation are as vast as the void. Before each trial begins, your wizard will select a loadout of three starting Arcana to use on their run, choosing from any of the six magical schools.

To start, you’ll pick one Basic Arcana (a workhorse cantrip you can cast as often as you like), one Signature Arcana (a more powerful ability; it also charges up a bar as you use it, eventually unleashing a mega-destructive ultimate form), and one Standard Arcana (a potent spell with a longer cooldown).

If you want all area-of-effect Fire Arcana, go for it. If you see what happens when you mix Water and Lighting, it’s your funeral. Want to try a trio of melee Arcana? Just the longest-range spells you can find? Want to try immortalizing your build as a meme? It’s up to you…just keep in mind that you’ll have opportunities to add two more Arcana to your arsenal during your trial, which could completely change your tactics and survival odds. A good wizard knows how to improvise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/d2682c55e9b0b64569def1ac8efa41a0a152e00b.png[/img]

[h3]The Trial Begins[/h3]

Once you’ve selected your initial Arcana loadout, it’s time to pass through the portal into the Floating Lands to see what gleeful carnage the council has concocted to test you. Every wizard begins their trial in the same place—an enchanted, but not exactly enchanting, jungle—but individual paths soon diverge, as chambers, portals, monsters, and challenging events are reconfigured between each run according to the council’s whims and Nazradin’s geomantic talents.

What might a wizard encounter, you wonder? Here’s just a sample of the Floating Lands’ myriad challenges and boons…

[list]
[*] A chamber full of monstrous flora and fauna that must be defeated in order to bring down a magical barrier.
[*] The mysterious Nox, an eerily familiar merchant who’ll offer you a choice of powerful, trial-changing, probably cursed Relics to use on your run.
[*] A raucous, gladiatorial clash with wizard council member Serjik…and considering your health after the contest, it’s a bit unclear whether he’s helping you or hindering you.
[*] A rival NPC wizard specializing in Earth magic—defeat her, and perhaps she’ll drop one of her own Arcana to add to your arsenal for the remainder of your run.
[*] An enchanted chest that tries to kill you. Oooh, that’s bad. But there’s an Arcana held within. That’s good! The Arcana is a terrible mismatch for your current loadout. That’s bad. But you can transmute the Arcana into gold to purchase a useful Relic later on. That’s good! The Relic is also cursed. That’s…bad? (You can go now.)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/30f0528cfad39515aff53886ea01c354f9f0da4f.png[/img]

At the end of each realm of the Floating Lands, every wizard must face off against its powerful boss, drawing upon all of their Arcana skill, dodging prowess, and dwindling health pool to advance to the next realm. Each realm has its own new environment, challenges, monsters, and nefarious ways to ruin a wizard’s day. 

But one wizard’s demise is the next wizard’s opportunity! And when you die, the cycle begins anew. Only this time, your skill has increased. You can dodge that golem’s attack with 96.3% proficiency. You’ve amassed more Chaos Gems to feed to Aletheia’s Apparatus, giving you an edge that your unlucky predecessor didn’t have. And you’ve got an awesome idea for a frost-themed build inspired by that blue wizard bastard who turned you into a block of ice….

Perhaps this time you’ll become…the Wizard of Legend 2!

[hr][/hr]
[i]Wizard of Legend 2 is currently in development, and Dead Mage is constantly iterating, testing, and gathering feedback—the gameplay and features discussed here are subject to change, and Dead Mage would love to hear what you think.

For more articles and posts like these and to be part of the conversation, follow Wizard of Legend 2 on [url=https://twitter.com/wizardoflegend2]X[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/WizardOfLegend]Facebook[/url], and [url=https://www.instagram.com/wizardoflegend2/]Instagram[/url], and join the community on [url=http://discord.gg/XFdenm5qkt]Discord[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Devlog #1: April 2024
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/6db5c874c72e5599ee7b0454c9ce1478f6f41bae.png[/img]
It’s official! Earlier this week, we released our latest trailer for Wizard of Legend 2 during the iii-Initiative Showcase, and we’re so excited to finally be sharing more about the game with you after revealing it way back in May of last year. We felt that this would be a great time to kick off a dev log series leading up to launch, so that everyone in the community can learn more about what we’re conjuring up behind the scenes, and gain some insights from the development team here at Dead Mage.

[previewyoutube=Dw__6PIbPO4;full][/previewyoutube]
As a team, we quickly fell in love with the fast-paced combat of the first game. We were eager to take on the challenge of bringing this sequel to life, while also ensuring Wizard of Legend’s trademark fluidity remains intact. We knew the responsive controls and quick movement that players have become so familiar with would be of the utmost importance. This motivated the team to find the perfect balance between maintaining and enhancing the gameplay, variety of Arcana, and controls for Wizard of Legend 2.

One of the first challenges we encountered was figuring out how to keep things fast, yet under control, considering the vast variety of Arcana available to players. This hurdle was initially a tough one for the team, and Senior Game Designer Javid Najibzadeh shared a few of his thoughts on how we approached it:

“We realized that we did need to make the animations much more snappy, making the anticipation animations much shorter - down to even a couple of frames at some points. The entire process of casting an Arcana needed to be faster in order to match the first game’s pace.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/e8895be1eb65ccb88df3859d3e4d5e0db4363fe6.gif[/img]
Speaking of Arcana, we’ve put in extra time and effort to make sure every spell has a unique feel, to make the gameplay more immersive. To do this, we ensured each one of the over 70 different Arcana have distinct abilities, controls, and nuances that will affect gameplay. This is still an ongoing process that we will continue to revise and work on as the game’s development progresses toward launch. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/e68e9ea5b98ef6566dfe34a95ce6f523c1dbb1f5.gif[/img]
One interesting decision we’ve made was to implement a skill that lets players double dash, but only over pits. Javid explains,

“We thought it might be a good idea to give players an extra chance of avoiding pits as it sometimes was too grim to fall into pits when you wanted to avoid being hit… At some point we removed it and every tester went almost mad.” 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/b4a1e457acc97a8fd8f2333baee82a755ec1230e.gif[/img]

This led to us reworking the skill to become a permanent progression upgrade, which ended up getting a positive response during our internal playtests.

However, after further playtesting, we felt the cooldown and other restrictions of dash Arcana made them less predictable, which affected the game’s pacing in a negative way. Due to this, we decided to replace dash Arcana with Relics that grant the same powers. If you’ve never played Wizard of Legend before, Relics are returning items in Wizard of Legend 2 that you can acquire as you progress through the Trials. These items will alter and enhance your abilities, but be careful what you decide to pick up! Some Relics may carry negative effects in addition to their benefits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/21801248090867ab509076c5e479228fa9561542.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44126579/a2bd27c9406a3b4dcae92ce74ae52a357ede62f3.jpg[/img]

These Relics will appeal to players who loved the dash Arcana from the first game while opening up opportunities for interesting builds. 

We are excited to reveal even more about Wizard of Legend 2 in the coming weeks, and we’re grateful for all of you who have been sharing your own excitement and interest with us on social media, as well as in our [url=https://discord.gg/P4rGgMr3]Discord server[/url]. So brace yourselves and get ready to engage in fast-paced combat with unique Arcana, encounter familiar and new NPCs, and claim the coveted title of Wizard of Legend!

We’ll see you next month, where we’ll be taking a closer look at Arcana design! If there are topics you’d like to see us explore in future dev logs, be sure to let us know by sharing your suggestions with us in Discord.
